---
title: "Governed Training and Learning-Compute Topology"
unit_id: "unit-20"
---

## The Checkpoint That Loaded Perfectly

The repository stack begins learning from its patch history. It trains a model
to predict which dependency changes will require source edits, which tests are
likely to fail, and which rollback plan fits the release topology.

Halfway through the run, a worker fails. The orchestrator loads the latest
weight checkpoint on replacement hardware. The file digest matches, the model
produces sensible outputs, and the loss resumes near its previous value. The
run is labeled recovered.

It is not the same run.

The optimizer momentum was not restored. The scheduler restarted one phase
early. The data sampler repeated part of the curriculum and skipped another
part. Random-number state changed. One retrieval cache was rebuilt from newer
documents. The distributed reduction order changed with the replacement
topology. The weights loaded; the adaptive process diverged.

This distinction matters even when the final model appears good. The system
cannot compare the resumed trajectory with the planned experiment as though
nothing changed. It cannot attribute an improvement to the optimizer while the
curriculum and topology also changed. It cannot reproduce the model from a
weight file that omits the process state that created it.

Governed Training gives the run a complete identity and transaction boundary.
Learning–Compute Topology widens the object under governance. Learning may
occur in model parameters, semantic memory, procedures, tools, evaluators,
environments, routing policies, or institutions. It may involve one persistent
learner, many competing lineages, or thousands of proposal workers feeding one
central state. Hardware count does not reveal that organization.

## A Training Run Is an Experimental Transaction

A run begins with a frozen contract. It names purpose, hypotheses, model and
learning-process identities, data and curriculum, optimizer and schedules,
topology, numerical policy, random seeds, resource budget, checkpoints,
evaluation, selection, authority, stop conditions, recovery, and non-claims.

The contract does not prevent every adaptation. It distinguishes planned
degrees of freedom from changes that create a new run, branch, or amendment.
Learning-rate tuning within a prospectively declared range may belong to one
campaign. Changing the data population after inspecting results does not.

Run identity persists across distributed workers and time. Every artifact
links to the same contract version or an explicit descendant. Logs, weights,
optimizer shards, evaluations, interventions, failures, and checkpoints are
events in the run, not loose files sharing a directory.

The transaction is append-only. A failed attempt remains in the denominator.
An operator intervention records what changed and why. A restart does not
overwrite the earlier trajectory. A selected checkpoint retains the family of
candidates from which it was chosen.

This makes a training result challengeable. A reviewer can ask whether the
reported outcome came from the frozen process, a valid amendment, or an
unacknowledged change.

## Data Order Is Part of the Mechanism

A dataset is not just a bag of examples. Selection, filtering, weighting,
deduplication, ordering, mixing, augmentation, replay, and curriculum can
change the learning trajectory.

The data record binds source, license and rights, provenance, transformations,
population, exclusions, splits, contamination checks, order policy, sampler
state, versions, and deletion obligations. It distinguishes data available to
training, validation, checkpoint selection, and final qualification.

The repository learner may begin with simple manifest-only changes, then move
to multi-file patches, rollback incidents, and ambiguous dependency graphs.
That curriculum can improve optimization or bias the system toward easy
patterns. The schedule is a hypothesis, not invisible loader configuration.

Distributed loaders need one global accounting. Each example or batch receives
an identity sufficient to detect unintended repeat, omission, or split
crossing. Dynamic filtering and online data acquisition produce events that
can be reconstructed. Privacy and deletion requests propagate to derivatives,
checkpoints, and later unlearning routes without claiming complete erasure.

Data quality remains task-relative. A perfectly tracked corpus can teach the
wrong objective. Provenance and order make the process inspectable; they do
not establish usefulness, consent, fairness, or truth.

## Optimizers Carry State and Policy

An optimizer maps evidence from the current computation into a state change.
Its state may include moments, factorizations, curvature estimates, schedules,
scalers, trust ratios, preconditioners, and parameter-group policy.

Changing optimizer is not a cosmetic implementation swap. It changes the
update rule, memory, communication, numerical sensitivity, and often the
meaning of hyperparameters. Restoring weights without optimizer state does not
continue the same trajectory.

The optimizer policy card records algorithm and version, equations or
reference implementation, parameter grouping, precision, schedules, clipping,
regularization, distributed semantics, checkpoint state, tuning budget,
failure triggers, and fallback. A primary method and ordinary baseline receive
matched tuning and rescue resources.

No optimizer wins universally. Adam, AdamW, Adafactor, LAMB, Shampoo, K-FAC,
Lion, Sophia, SOAP, schedule-free methods, Muon, and future methods trade memory,
communication, curvature approximation, scale transfer, stability, and
hardware fit. Source-reported gains enter as hypotheses and comparators, not
local evidence.

The stack should choose an optimizer because it meets the run contract under
complete cost, not because its update looks theoretically elegant or has
frontier branding.

## Randomness and Numerics Are Named Inputs

Random initialization, sampling, dropout, augmentation, routing, kernel
selection, and asynchronous order can all affect a run. Seeds help reproduce
some choices but are not a universal replay mechanism.

The run inventories random-number generators, seed derivation, per-worker
streams, state checkpoints, and nondeterministic operations. It records
precision, rounding, reduction order, compiler and kernel versions, and
hardware properties where they can alter the result.

Exact bitwise replay may be infeasible or unnecessary. The contract chooses an
equivalence class before the run: exact artifact, bounded numerical deviation,
matched trajectory statistics, or outcome-level equivalence. Tolerances include
the consumer and consequence.

Determinism can cost throughput and still omit environmental change. Nondeterminism
can be acceptable if the distribution is characterized and checkpoint
selection does not exploit lucky seeds. Neither label establishes quality.

Repeated runs retain variance. A single favorable seed cannot represent a
method. Failed and unstable runs remain in the denominator, including attempts
terminated before a headline metric.

## Distributed Execution Is Not Learning Topology

Data, tensor, pipeline, sequence, expert, and optimizer-state parallelism
describe how computation and state are mapped across devices. They matter for
communication, memory, synchronization, failure, and numerical behavior.

They do not determine how many adaptive identities exist.

Eight GPUs can compute gradients for one synchronized model. They are eight
workers and one persistent learner. The same eight GPUs can host four lineages
that see different environments and are later selected or merged. They are
four adaptive identities. Hundreds of workers can evaluate perturbations while
one central vector receives every update. Proposal width is large and durable
learning width is one.

Conversely, one device can time-share many persistent learners. Counting
processes, agents, or chips does not reveal where experience accumulates, who
judges it, which state changes, or what survives integration.

This separation lets the system optimize execution without silently changing
the learning process. Moving a synchronized update to a faster collective may
preserve semantics within tolerance. Replacing independent branches with
gradient averaging may destroy the very diversity the experiment was designed
to test.

## Four Topologies Must Stay Separate

Model architecture describes how one model computes and represents: attention,
recurrence, state space, graph operations, symbolic rules, or another
substrate.

Learning-process topology describes persistent adaptive identities and the
relations among evidence, judgment, credit, state change, integration, and
authority.

Execution topology maps operations and state to processes, devices, services,
memory, and time.

Physical compute topology describes actual hardware, interconnect, storage,
energy, failure domains, and geography.

These objects interact but do not inherit properties automatically. A highly
parallel execution can implement a centralized learner. A decentralized
learning process can run sequentially. A modular model can be trained through
one global objective. A monolithic model can participate in a population of
competing lineages.

Governance needs the distinctions because authority and failure follow
different edges. A device operator can restart hardware without authority to
merge adaptive branches. A learning controller can retire a branch without
permission to publish its weights. A model update can be valid while the
physical infrastructure violates a resource or jurisdiction constraint.

## Adaptive Identity Is Persistent Causal State

An adaptive identity is a stateful process whose history can influence future
behavior and whose changes are separately attributable enough for the current
decision.

Identity can reside in parameters, optimizer state, memory, procedures,
datasets, evaluators, routing policy, environment, or institutional rules. A
model replica that contributes to one synchronized state is usually not an
independent learner. A memory branch that accumulates distinct evidence may be.

The identity record names state, lineage, observations, judgments, credit,
updates, authority, checkpoints, descendants, integration, and retirement. It
also names ambiguity. Some systems do not admit one clean boundary; the record
can preserve competing decompositions rather than force a false count.

Identity is task-relative. Two branches may be distinct for causal analysis
but operationally equivalent for a consumer. A topology representation should
state why the distinction matters.

Without persistent identity, credit cannot be assigned honestly. Improvement
after a merge may come from one branch, the interaction among branches, the
evaluator, or changed data. A final score alone cannot recover that history.

## Learning Relations Need Types

An unlabeled arrow between components hides what moves. Learning–Compute
Topology uses typed relations such as evidence, judgment, credit, state,
artifact, control, and authority.

Evidence carries observations or measurements. Judgment evaluates evidence
under a method. Credit assigns consequence to a state, action, component, or
process. State edges mutate durable adaptive state. Artifact edges produce or
consume models, memories, tools, and records. Control schedules or selects
processes. Authority permits, denies, narrows, or retires change.

These relations should not collapse. An evaluator’s judgment is not credit
until a policy assigns it. Credit is not an update until an authorized learning
rule changes state. A produced checkpoint is not qualified for use. A controller
that can schedule a branch may lack authority to promote it.

Typed edges expose bottlenecks and capture. Many proposal workers may feed one
evaluator, creating judgment concentration. Several evaluators may depend on
one evidence source. Distributed credit may still commit through one authority
node.

The topology can then be challenged at the relation that matters instead of
calling the whole process centralized or decentralized.

## LCT-IR Makes the Process Explicit

Learning–Compute Topology Intermediate Representation, or LCT-IR, is a typed
description of adaptive identities, state classes, relation edges,
constraints, lifecycle events, and semantic obligations.

It is not a graph drawing format. The representation should distinguish
persistent from transient state, evidence from control, proposed from committed
change, local from shared state, and semantic identity from execution placement.
Validators reject missing endpoints, invalid relation roles, authority
widening, and incompatible lifecycle states.

The source package’s bounded reference implementation parses, validates,
normalizes, compares, and compiles selected LCT-IR objects. Its eleven unit
tests passing establishes that finite implementation behavior under those
tests. It does not establish that the primitive set is complete, that two human
encoders will agree, or that the representation improves training.

An IR earns adoption when independent teams can encode natural processes,
disagreements reveal useful ambiguity, interventions map to executable changes,
and the representation predicts or controls outcomes better than simpler
descriptions.

## Learning Causal Normal Form Is a Comparison Tool

A normalized learning process can be expressed around adaptive identities and
the path from evidence to judgment, credit, state mutation, integration, and
authority. Normalization makes processes comparable even when frameworks and
hardware differ.

The proposed Learning Causal Normal Form is not claimed as the unique canonical
representation of all learning. It is a hypothesis about a useful sufficient
vocabulary under explicit-state and interface assumptions.

Normalization should preserve the distinctions relevant to the consumer. Two
execution plans may normalize to the same learning process if device placement
does not alter the declared semantics. Two visually similar loops should remain
different if one preserves competing lineages and the other averages them away.

Information loss is recorded. An opaque proprietary service may expose only
aggregate judgment, leaving credit assignment unknown. A physical process may
have hidden state. The normal form should represent an unresolved boundary,
not invent internal edges.

The value of normalization is empirical: better audit, prediction,
intervention, portability, or design. A neat canonical graph is not itself an
outcome.

## The Semantic Compiler Needs a Firewall

The semantic topology must eventually become an execution plan. Compilation
maps adaptive identities, relations, state, and constraints onto software,
devices, collectives, storage, and schedules.

A semantic compiler firewall protects obligations during lowering. It checks
that identity is not merged accidentally, state is not shared beyond scope,
authority does not widen, required independence is not lost, evidence remains
traceable, budgets hold, and recovery stays reachable.

Some transformations are semantics-preserving under stated assumptions:
sharding one state, batching evidence, or replacing a collective. Others are
semantic amendments: changing branch communication, evaluator ownership,
credit policy, or integration rule.

The compiler emits an obligation report, not merely executable configuration.
It names preserved relations, introduced dependencies, approximations,
unresolved constraints, physical failure domains, and required validation.

Compilation success establishes conformance to encoded rules. It cannot prove
that the semantic specification was correct or that hardware will realize the
model faithfully.

## Realization Leakage Is a Measured Residual

Physical realization can change the learning process through latency,
bandwidth, synchronization, precision, failure, scheduling, memory pressure,
and locality.

A theoretically independent branch may share a cache, data service, evaluator,
or failure domain. An asynchronous update may systematically favor fast
workers. Compression can erase rare evidence. Limited cut capacity can prevent
the information flow assumed by the semantic topology.

Realization leakage compares the declared process with observed execution. It
tracks delayed or dropped evidence, altered order, stale state, approximated
judgment, credit distortion, shared dependencies, and unauthorized control
paths.

Some leakage is acceptable within a frozen tolerance. Some changes the
experimental question. The run record classifies the difference and prevents
an altered realization from inheriting the original claim silently.

Topology metrics such as adaptive width, evidence diversity, judgment
concentration, credit bottlenecks, integration loss, authority concentration,
and cut capacity can help describe this gap. Their usefulness must be tested
against simpler counts and actual outcomes.

## Checkpoints Are Full-State Commits

A complete checkpoint inventories every state class required to continue the
declared process: model parameters, optimizer, scheduler, sampler, RNG,
precision scaler, curriculum, data position, topology, memory, caches,
adapters, evaluator state, policy, environment, and pending external work.

The inventory is framework- and process-specific. The contract says which
classes exist and why. Atomicity binds mutually dependent shards to one commit.
Digests, versions, provenance, and storage receipts make substitution or
partial restoration detectable.

A weight-and-step summary is not injective over complete run state. Distinct
optimizer, sampler, or topology states can share the same visible pair. No
universal decoder can reconstruct omitted state from those fields.

Loading is therefore the start of recovery, not its conclusion. The system
restores all declared classes, checks cross-state consistency, exercises a
prospectively chosen equivalence test, and records unknowns. If equivalence
fails, the restart becomes a branch or new attempt.

Full-state checkpointing can be expensive. The design should compare storage,
coordination, and recovery value; use incremental or tiered methods where they
preserve the contract; and narrow equivalence rather than claiming impossible
exactness.

## Resume Equivalence Is Prospective

Two trajectories are equivalent only relative to a declared consumer and
tolerance. Exact optimizer research may need closely matched updates. A broad
capability campaign may accept statistical equivalence. A production recovery
may care about output and safety envelopes more than identical weights.

The equivalence test is frozen before failure. Otherwise the team can select a
metric that makes the restart look continuous. It includes positive controls,
known divergent states, time horizon, and stop conditions.

Recovery compares uninterrupted and resumed paths where feasible. It reports
which state was restored, what changed, and whether the resumed path remains
eligible for the original analysis. A successful outcome can still be a
non-equivalent trajectory.

Distributed faults complicate atomicity. Workers may observe different commit
states, storage can lag, and external data may move. The protocol chooses
coordination and consistency according to consequence and records residual
windows rather than asserting perfect recovery.

## Checkpoint Selection Is Not Qualification

Validation can choose among checkpoints without authorizing deployment or
support. The selection set and rule are frozen, and every candidate remains in
the family record.

Repeatedly checking a final holdout while tuning checkpoints contaminates it.
Choosing the best seed or time step and reporting only that result hides
variance and selection cost. Early stopping is a policy with its own evidence,
not an innocent implementation detail.

Qualification uses an independently unopened population and separate decision
authority. It measures the complete capability and risk contract, including
recovery and cost. A training service hands a candidate to qualification; it
cannot promote its own model.

This separation also protects negative results. A failed qualification should
not be rewritten as training failure if the instrument was inadequate. The
evidence system classifies what the run and evaluator were competent to show.

## Scaling Is a Family of Interventions

“Scale” can mean more parameters, data, tokens, training time, context, memory,
workers, proposals, branches, environments, evaluators, tools, or physical
resources. These interventions are not interchangeable.

A scaling study freezes the changed variables, held variables, data population,
architecture, optimizer, topology, quality target, resources, and forecast
before running. It reports the complete attempt family and uncertainty, not
only the largest successful point.

Time-to-quality can be more informative than final quality when methods consume
different resources. The report includes accelerator and host work, memory,
communication, storage, data preparation, failures, checkpointing, evaluation,
human tuning, and discarded runs. Hardware utilization is not useful learning
unless the system reaches the contracted outcome.

Transfer needs separate axes. A hyperparameterization that transfers across
width may not transfer across depth, duration, architecture, data regime, or
learning topology. A distributed schedule that works on one interconnect may
fail elsewhere. The receipt states the tested regime and expires when material
variables change.

Scaling curves describe observations under a family. They do not identify a
mechanism by themselves. A threshold-like jump can arise from metric
resolution, data change, selection, prompting, tool use, or topology. Mechanism
claims require interventions that separate these alternatives.

The topology view expands scaling science. Increasing proposal workers while
holding one commitment state changes exploration width. Increasing persistent
branches changes adaptive diversity. Adding evaluators changes judgment
capacity. Widening communication changes integration and correlated failure.
The same compute budget can therefore implement causally different scaling
experiments.

## Topology Claims Need Causal Experiments

A topology diagram can explain a process after the fact without predicting
anything. To earn causal status, the representation should support prospective
interventions with directional predictions.

An experiment can hold model architecture, data, optimizer, evaluation, and
total resources approximately fixed while changing one learning relation:
centralized versus distributed judgment, isolated versus communicating
branches, local versus global credit, selection versus averaging, or one
authority gate versus delegated integration.

The intervention packet states which LCT-IR edge or node changes, expected
information flow, predicted learning and failure outcomes, realization plan,
confounders, and equivalence checks. It verifies that the physical execution
actually implemented the semantic difference.

Outcomes include capability, generalization, calibration, diversity,
catastrophic failure, information retained through integration, response to
corruption, recovery, cost, and human burden. A topology may improve one and
worsen another.

Ablations also test the representation itself. Remove relation types, merge
adaptive identities, or replace the topology with worker count and generic
graphs. If predictions and decisions do not deteriorate, the added vocabulary
has not earned its complexity.

Independent encoders should receive the same process artifacts and produce
their own topology records. Agreement is not expected on every ambiguous
boundary. Useful disagreement should identify missing evidence or consumer-
relative identity, not arbitrary annotation preference.

## Learning Extends Beyond Parameters

The repository stack can improve without changing model weights. It can add a
dated fact to semantic memory, qualify a procedure, strengthen a test, revise
a router, update an evaluator, change an environment, or amend an institutional
policy.

Each locus has different persistence, verification, reach, deletion, and
rollback. A memory entry is inspectable and easy to expire but may not affect
behavior reliably. A procedure changes action directly but can be scoped and
retired. Parameter updates generalize implicitly but are hard to interpret and
remove. An evaluator update changes which future evidence is admitted. An
institutional policy can constrain many systems while carrying legitimacy and
implementation burdens.

Learning topology therefore includes state outside the training framework.
Evidence from a failed patch may lead to a test rather than a gradient. Human
review may change the task ontology. A legal decision may remove an otherwise
effective data or deployment route.

These loci can interact. A memory supplies context to a model; a procedure
generates traces used for training; an evaluator selects model checkpoints; a
policy determines which feedback is admissible. The topology records these
causal edges so a later correction can reach descendants.

Not every change should be synchronized. Local memory can preserve minority or
domain knowledge that global parameters would flatten. A central policy can
protect rights that local optimization would trade away. Multiple time scales
and authorities are a design feature, not an inconsistency to average.

Unit 21 will govern the commitment decision across these loci. For training,
the important consequence is that a model run is one adaptive process inside a
larger system, not the universal location of learning.

## Adaptive Branch–Validate–Integrate

One proposed topology, Adaptive Branch–Validate–Integrate, preserves multiple
candidate lineages, subjects them to independent validation, and commits only
admissible changes through a governed integration boundary.

Branching creates diversity only if histories, evidence, or mechanisms differ
meaningfully. Copies with different random seeds may still share the decisive
failure. Validation needs independent evidence and complete candidate custody.
Integration can select, merge, distill, compose, archive, or reject; each route
has different information loss.

The governor controls branch creation, resources, communication, evaluation,
integration, rollback, and retirement. Candidates cannot alter the gate that
judges them. Failed branches remain evidence rather than disappearing from the
denominator.

ABVI is a research proposal, not an implemented improvement result. It should
compete with one-lineage training, ordinary checkpoint search, population-based
training, evolutionary strategies, federated learning, and simple ensembles
under matched resources and outcomes.

## One Repository Learner, One Governed Run

The training contract freezes the repository task population, curriculum,
data rights, model, optimizer policy, seeds, distributed execution, LCT-IR
topology, checkpoints, resume test, evaluation, selection, and qualification
handoff.

The declared learning topology contains one persistent model lineage, a dated
semantic-memory store, a procedure candidate branch, two evaluators, and one
integration authority. Evidence from patch outcomes reaches the evaluators.
Their judgments assign separate credit to model, memory, and procedure changes.
No component can commit itself.

Execution maps the process across eight workers. A topology change replaces
synchronous data parallelism with four persistent branches sharing two
evaluators. That is a semantic amendment, not merely performance tuning. The
run forks under a new contract and preserves the prior attempt.

A worker failure triggers full-state recovery. The weight file loads, but the
sampler and optimizer mismatch the checkpoint family. The system refuses
equivalent-resume status and records a new branch. It can continue useful work
without laundering the experiment.

At the end, validation selects a checkpoint family. The final qualification
set remains unopened. The run has produced a candidate and evidence, not a
deployment decision.

## Training Authority Expires

A run consumes data, compute, infrastructure, evaluator attention, and often
the right to create powerful or sensitive artifacts. Its authority is bounded
by purpose, population, capability, resource, duration, security, and release
policy.

The controller can schedule admitted work but cannot widen those limits. A
promising loss curve does not authorize more data, a larger capability domain,
or publication. Material changes route to an accountable amendment or new run.

Stop conditions include resource ceilings, invalid data custody, contamination,
unexpected capability, unstable or unsafe behavior, checkpoint inconsistency,
loss of observation, and evidence that the instrument cannot answer the
question. Stopping preserves artifacts and residuals for review; it is not a
failed optimization event to hide.

Emergency intervention can pause workers, revoke credentials, isolate
checkpoints, or preserve a safe baseline. The operator records the exact state
and authority used. Resumption requires fresh custody rather than an automatic
job retry.

At closure, unused grants expire, sensitive artifacts receive disposition,
costs and failures remain in the denominator, and every candidate enters
qualification, archive, quarantine, or retirement. Training success alone
cannot select the release route.

The closure receipt is therefore an evidence handoff, not a certificate that
the resulting learner is useful, safe, general, robust, or ready.

## Failure Cases

**Weight-file identity.** Loading parameters is called continuation.

**Sampler amnesia.** Repeated or skipped data disappears from the record.

**Optimizer reset.** Lost moments or schedules silently create a new
trajectory.

**Seed theater.** Recording one seed implies reproducibility despite
nondeterministic kernels and environment changes.

**Failed-run erasure.** Only the selected checkpoint and successful attempts
survive.

**Validation leakage.** Checkpoint selection consumes the qualification set.

**Topology collapse.** Device count is mistaken for adaptive-identity count.

**Unlabeled edge.** Evidence, judgment, credit, state, control, and authority
become generic communication.

**Replica diversity.** Copies of one state are treated as independent
learners.

**Semantic compiler drift.** Faster realization merges branches or shares
state that the specification kept distinct.

**Hidden realization leakage.** Latency, precision, or failure changes credit
and evidence flow.

**Metric ontology.** Attractive topology measures substitute for outcome
improvement.

**Integration survivor bias.** Failed branches vanish, making selection look
inevitable.

**Scaling by endpoint.** Final loss or capability hides total attempts,
compute, data, failures, and selection.

**Self-qualification.** The training controller promotes the model it created.

## The Strongest Simpler Baseline

The strongest baseline uses an ordinary reproducible training manifest,
experiment tracker, distributed framework, full framework checkpoint,
versioned data loader, fixed evaluation, and human-reviewed promotion.

That baseline should remain preferred unless LCT adds explanatory or control
value. Many runs have one obvious persistent learner and need no elaborate
topology IR. Existing workflow and lineage tools may capture enough state.

Comparison should measure independent encoding agreement, defects found,
intervention precision, causal attribution, recovery, transfer across
frameworks, prediction of failure and cost, human comprehension, implementation
burden, and learning outcomes. Graph complexity or vocabulary coverage is not
success.

If the topology layer merely redescribes standard training, it should contract
to a small extension of the run manifest.

## What the Current Work Establishes

Governed Model Training has three implemented public targets through 20 Lean
declarations. One authored transaction fixture, schema, and independent
semantic validator check 21 transaction mutations, seven weight-only omitted-
state collisions, and nine complete-encoding mutations. The finite model
establishes run-handoff, complete-checkpoint, selection-separation, and
checkpoint-information consequences over authored records. It does not train
a model or establish resume equivalence, optimizer quality, distributed fault
tolerance, scaling, or deployment.

The natural five-arm campaign is prospectively specified and unexecuted. No
outcome from it is reported here.

Learning–Compute Topology contributes a complete source package, seven bounded
mathematical propositions, a reference LCT-IR implementation whose supplied
suite passes 11 of 11 tests, manually coded scoped coverage and novelty
matrices, toy or analytical phase diagrams, and the ABVI proposal. The seven
propositions have not been independently mechanized in this repository. The
implementation covers bounded IR behavior, not neural training, distributed
execution, online topology control, prediction, safety, or superiority.

The joined chapter therefore establishes a precise training and topology
contract with bounded executable and formal artifacts. It does not establish
that the topology representation improves learning or that the combined system
works in a natural campaign.

## From a Minimum Run Record to Adaptive Infrastructure

A minimum implementation can use the repository learner. Freeze one run,
inventory full state, inject optimizer, sampler, RNG, topology, and cache
omissions, restore from a checkpoint, and classify equivalence under a
prospective test. Preserve all attempts and keep qualification unopened.

Encode the same process independently in LCT-IR. Compare disagreements, then
compile it onto two execution topologies. Inject branch merging, shared
evaluator dependence, stale evidence, cut-capacity limits, and authority
widening. Measure whether the IR detects changes that an ordinary manifest
misses.

The next stage needs matched natural campaigns comparing the strong training-
manifest baseline with LCT-assisted design. Vary one persistent learner,
populations, proposal-worker systems, federation, and ABVI. Hold model, data,
resources, evaluation, and authority constant where the question permits.

A mature learning infrastructure would treat model, memory, procedure, tool,
evaluator, environment, and institution updates as one typed topology. It would
compile semantic learning plans to changing hardware, observe realization
leakage, recover complete state, preserve failed branches, and hand candidates
to independent qualification.

## The Strongest Objection

Learning–Compute Topology may be a new vocabulary for familiar workflow graphs,
distributed training, population methods, and experiment tracking. More typed
nodes can increase documentation while changing no prediction or decision.

The objection is correct unless the representation earns its layer. The book
does not claim universal canonicality or completeness. The layer should be as
small as the consumer requires.

Its value proposition is falsifiable: independent encoders should agree enough
to support action; disagreements should expose real ambiguity; topology
interventions should predictably change evidence, credit, persistence, or
outcomes; and semantic compilation should prevent consequential realization
drift at acceptable cost.

If ordinary manifests and experiment trackers match those outcomes, use them.

## Evidence That Would Change the Conclusion

The topology layer should narrow if independent encoders cannot identify stable
adaptive identities or typed relations, if its metrics fail to predict or
explain relevant outcomes, or if matched-resource interventions show no control
or recovery benefit.

Support would require prospectively frozen natural learning campaigns,
competent simple baselines, independent topology encoding, causal ablations,
multiple frameworks and hardware realizations, complete resource and human
costs, reproduction, and transfer. ABVI must compete with ordinary training,
search, population, and evolutionary methods rather than inherit plausibility.

The training contract should also narrow where framework-native checkpointing
and versioning produce equal run identity, recovery, selection discipline, and
audit at lower cost.

## What This Establishes

A learning run is a full-state experimental transaction, not a weight file.
Data order, optimizer, randomness, numerics, topology, checkpoints, resume,
selection, and qualification belong to its identity.

Model architecture, learning-process topology, execution topology, and
physical compute topology are different objects. Typed evidence, judgment,
credit, state, artifact, control, and authority relations make adaptation
challengeable. Semantic compilation must expose realization leakage.

The current repository establishes finite training-record semantics and a
bounded LCT-IR implementation. It does not establish natural training or
topology advantage.

Training produces experiences, scores, failures, and candidate lessons. Unit
21 asks the harder question: what durable thing, if anything, should change;
where should it persist; and how should it later be corrected, forgotten, or
unlearned?
